main_text.p: nem, tum sacerdotium. Sufficit eidem sub-jecto applicari, prout ex resurrectione il-lius, & honore sacerdotali, Christi filiatio æterna sequebatur. Veteres autem de [ἐνανθρωπήσει[?]] quando illis vox hodie, [χρον-χὴν ἀποφαντικόν[?]] denotabat. Ita locus ille Habacuci Cap. II. 4, [ὁ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται[?]] ad fidem justificantem, ejusque fructum trahitur, ut scriptori ad Hebræos Cap. x, 38, sic Paulo ad Romanos Cap. i, 17. & Galatas Cap. iii. ii. Quanquam Pro-phetæ in speciem, non de Evangelicâ illa virtute, sed legali verius, integritate, constantia, nec de salute, sed liberatione ex Babylonis servitute. Sic Psaltis ille lo-cus, de sessione ad dextram, Psalm. cx,1. de glorioso Christi regno exponitur, cita-turque, ut Hebr. i. 13, & x, 13. sic etiam 1. Corinth. xv, 25. Pariter Jeremiæ vati-cinium, de peccatis sub novo Fœdere tollendis, citatum authori Epistolæ, Capitibus viii. & x, Paulo itidem allegatur, ad Romanos Cap. xi, 27. Sic, tentati Dei illud flagitium, Israëlitis pridem impa-ctum, in Christum admissum dicitur, quem-

page.notes: Greek words are hard to read at this scan resolution; the Greek forms are best readings and are marked [?]. The running head is blurred, especially "Authore", which is marked [?]. The "ii." after "Galatas Cap. iii." and the "i, 17." reference are as far as I can read them. Possible printing errors left as printed: "illc" is read as "ille"; "Cap. iii. ii." may be "Cap. iii. 11.".
